2609.17119.title: An Empirical Study of Counterfactual Self-Explanations in LLMs
2609.17119.paper_summary: Large language models can easily generate explanations for their own outputs, but such self-explanations are not necessarily faithful to the model's behavior. We study this issue through counterfactual self-explanations, where a model minimally edits an input so that its own prediction changes. Across sentiment analysis and natural language inference, we evaluate ten instruction-tuned models from the LLaMA-3 and Qwen-2.5 families, measuring faithfulness, minimality, and alignment with human-annotated rationales. Our results show that model scale is the strongest determinant of explanation quality: larger models are substantially more likely to generate counterfactuals that flip their own predictions and target decision-relevant evidence. In contrast, the rationale-guided condition produces edit-minimal counterfactuals that are also more human-aligned. However, it does not consistently improve faithfulness. Overall, counterfactual self-explanations can provide useful behavioral evidence about model decisions, but their reliability depends strongly on model capacity and should be empirically validated rather than assumed.
2609.17119.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型可以輕易生成對其輸出的解釋，但這些自我解釋不一定忠實於模型的行為。我們通過反事實自我解釋來研究這個問題，其中模型對輸入進行最小編輯，以便其自身的預測發生變化。在情感分析和自然語言推理中，我們評估了來自LLaMA-3和Qwen-2.5家族的十個指令調整模型，測量忠實性、最小性和與人類標註的理由的一致性。我們的結果顯示，模型規模是解釋質量的最強決定因素：較大的模型更有可能生成翻轉其自身預測的反事實，並針對決策相關的證據。相比之下，基於理由的條件產生的編輯最小反事實也更符合人類的期望。然而，它並未始終提高忠實性。總體而言，反事實自我解釋可以提供有關模型決策的有用行為證據，但其可靠性在很大程度上取決於模型的能力，應該經過實證驗證，而不是假設。
